subject: fix: skip missing doc_ids in Table.update and Table.remove (#616)
problem_statement:
fix: skip missing doc_ids in Table.update and Table.remove (#616)

`Table.get(doc_id=N)` and `Table.get(doc_ids=[N])` already return
silently when the requested document does not exist, but
`Table.update(doc_ids=[N])` and `Table.remove(doc_ids=[N])` raise
`KeyError`. The four code paths are documented and named symmetrically,
so the asymmetric behaviour is surprising and was raised as a bug in
issue #591.

Worse, when a mix of existing and missing IDs is passed to `update`,
the first existing documents are mutated in place before the
`KeyError` is raised. The storage write is then skipped by
`_update_table`, but documents are shared by reference between the
in-memory copy and the table dict, so subsequent reads still see the
half-applied update. The operation is neither atomic nor recoverable.

Filter the requested IDs against the live table *inside* the updater,
before performing any side effects, and return only the IDs that were
actually updated/removed. This:

* makes the four `get`/`update`/`remove` paths consistent;
* makes both operations atomic - either every existing target is
  affected, or none is;
* lets `upsert` drop its now-unreachable `except KeyError` branch
  (`update` simply returns `[]` when nothing matched, which falls
  through the existing `if updated_docs:` guard into the insert
  path).

Regression coverage is added in `tests/test_tinydb.py` for the missing,
mixed and cross-method-consistency cases.

Fixes #591

subject: Do not let raw building close a parent cycle (#3286)
problem_statement:
Do not let raw building close a parent cycle (#3286)

``InspectBuilder.object_build()`` re-parents nodes it finds in ``_done``
when the same live class shows up again under a different owner. A class
that exposes itself, or a sibling, as one of its own attributes therefore
ended up as its own ancestor, and ``NodeNG.root()`` spun forever on the
resulting loop.

pyo3 complex enums have exactly that shape: every variant is attached to
the enum class, so each variant sees itself and its siblings through
inheritance. Linting a project that imports such a module hung with 99%
of the time spent in the ``while parent.parent`` walk of ``root()``.

Only register the name when re-parenting would close a cycle.

Closes #3284

subject: Do not crash on an argument that repeats the name of a variadic one (#3260)
problem_statement:
Do not crash on an argument that repeats the name of a variadic one (#3260)

``Arguments.default_value()`` narrowed ``arguments`` to the non-variadic
arguments by dropping every entry whose name matched ``vararg`` or
``kwarg``. A name can be shared: ``def f(x, *y, y)`` and
``def f(x, *, y, **y)`` both parse, and only fail later at compile time
with "duplicate argument". The keyword-only ``y`` was dropped along with
the variadic one, so the offset used to index ``defaults`` was computed
from a list one entry too short and ``defaults[0]`` was read from an
empty list, raising ``IndexError`` through ``pylint``'s ``safe_infer``.

Build the list from ``posonlyargs`` and ``args`` instead, which holds
exactly the positional arguments, and offset it by ``defaults`` alone.
The keyword-only arguments are already handled by the ``kw_defaults``
lookup above. This also lets a positional default survive being shadowed:
``def f(y=1, *y)`` used to report no default at all.

Closes #3259

subject: Give the fallback ``__new__`` of the object model a usable signature
problem_statement:
Give the fallback ``__new__`` of the object model a usable signature

``ObjectModel.attr___new__`` is returned whenever the real ``__new__`` is
not found: ``instance.__new__``, ``super().__new__(cls)`` in a class with
an uninferable ancestor, and the ``__new__`` of C types outside
``builtins`` (reached through raw_building's ``ImportFrom``). It was
built from ``def __new__(self, cls)``, but ``BoundMethod`` treats
``__new__`` as taking the class explicitly (``implicit_parameters() ==
0``), so the class argument filled ``self`` and ``cls`` was reported as
missing, while any other argument was unexpected.

Use ``def __new__(cls, *args, **kwargs)`` instead, mirroring the
``__init__`` fallback next to it. Result inference is unchanged: it goes
through ``UnboundMethod._infer_builtin_new``, not the body.

Closes #3237

Fix crash on a dataclass base that annotates __init__ (#3206)

A class body can bind `__init__` to a name instead of a function by
annotating it as a dataclass field, as in `__init__: int`. astroid then
skips generating an `__init__` for that class, so its locals entry stays
an AssignName. _find_arguments_from_base_classes read `.args` off every
dataclass base's `__init__`, so a subclass of such a dataclass crashed
the transform with AttributeError: 'AssignName' object has no attribute
'args'.

Skip a base whose `__init__` is not a FunctionDef; it contributes no
arguments to the generated `__init__`.

Closes #3200

problem_statement:
Infer the value of a data descriptor as unknown

raw_building modelled a data descriptor of a C-implemented class as a
class named after the attribute, so reading such an attribute inferred
that class rather than a value: exc.__traceback__.tb_frame inferred a
tb_frame class and gen.gi_frame a gi_frame class. Attributes of the
frame those descriptors return were then reported as missing, e.g.
E1101 Class 'tb_frame' has no 'f_locals' member.

Build an unknown value instead, the same node the fallback branch of
InspectBuilder.object_build already uses for members astroid cannot
model. The attribute itself stays resolvable; only its value is now
Uninferable.

``__new__`` and write the slots directly, skipping the conditional
default handling in ``__init__`` that the caller immediately overwrites.

``path`` and ``constraints`` are independent copies, ``lookupname`` is
reset, the ``nodes_inferred`` counter stays shared, ``callcontext`` and
``boundnode`` carry over, and ``__init__`` is genuinely not called.
``TestInferenceContextInit`` covers the ``nodes_inferred`` parameter on

and typing.TypeAliasType instances, so report those qualified names, the way
#3137 did for Slice and builtins.slice.

Also add a test asserting that a node inferred as itself answers qname() and
pytype(), so the next such node cannot ship without them.

[perf] Cap oversized str/bytes and sequence concatenation during inference

the repetition operators are size-capped in const_infer_binary_op (*, <<) and _multiply_seq_by_int (*), but concatenation with + is not, and each operand can sit just under the cap. ("a" * 90000000) + ("b" * 90000000) is 34 source characters yet materializes a 180 MB Const string during inference, and chaining more + terms grows it without bound. the list/tuple path in tl_infer_binary_op is worse: _filter_uninferable_nodes infers every element of the concatenated sequence, so ([0] * 90000000) + ([0] * 90000000) walks ~1.8e8 elements. both + branches now yield Uninferable once the combined length passes 1e8, the additive analog of the existing repetition guards. small concatenations keep inferring their exact value.

Remove `asname` kwarg from Import/ImportFrom `_infer` (#3109)

* Remove ``asname`` kwarg from Import/ImportFrom ``_infer``

The ``asname`` keyword argument on ``Import._infer`` and
``ImportFrom._infer`` only switched whether ``self.real_name(name)`` was
applied to the ``lookupname`` before resolving the import. It was not
included in the inference cache key, so two semantically distinct calls
(default ``asname=True`` translating the alias to the underlying name vs
``asname=False`` resolving the raw alias) collapsed to the same cache
entry. Whichever ran first poisoned the result of the second.

This is the root cause of pylint-dev/pylint#10193: pylint's
``_infer_name_module`` calls ``node.infer(context, asname=False)`` to
fetch the unaliased module, but the prior ``asname=True`` traversal had
already cached the aliased module under the same key, so the
``asname=False`` lookup returned the wrong module and downstream
``no-name-in-module`` analysis raised a spurious E0611.

Hoist the ``real_name`` translation up to
``ImportNode._infer_name``, the per-statement hook invoked by
``_infer_stmts`` to choose ``context.lookupname`` before dispatching
``_infer``. With the translation done before ``infer()`` is reached:

* The standard ``Name`` inference flow (the only path that previously
  benefited from ``asname=True``) now lands on ``_infer`` with
  ``lookupname`` already translated to the real module name.
* Direct callers of ``Import.infer``/``ImportFrom.infer`` (the path
  pylint's ``_infer_name_module`` uses) receive the lookup name as-is,
  matching the old ``asname=False`` semantics. The ``asname`` kwarg is
  no longer accepted on ``_infer`` (``**kwargs`` swallows it for
  back-compatible call sites).
* The cache key (``(node, lookupname, callcontext, boundnode)``)
  differs between the two flows because their ``lookupname`` values
  differ, so the cross-flow collision is gone.

When ``real_name`` cannot find a matching alias, ``_infer_name`` returns
``None`` and ``_infer`` raises ``InferenceError`` on the resulting
``name is None`` guard, preserving the original handling of the
unresolvable-alias case (see pylint-dev/pylint#4692).

Add a regression test that exercises both flows on the same
``import os.path as os`` node in the order that previously triggered
the bug, and assert ``_infer_stmts`` yields ``os.path`` while the
direct ``infer`` call yields the raw stdlib ``os`` module.

Refs pylint-dev/pylint#10193
Closes #3007

* tests: hoist _infer_stmts import to module top to satisfy pylint

The regression test added in this PR imported _infer_stmts inside
the test method body, which trips pylint's import-outside-toplevel
rule (C0415) and breaks the pylint pre-commit hook in CI.

Move the import to the existing from astroid.bases import ... block
at the top of the file.

fix: avoid bootstrap crash on PyPy 7.3.22 (TypeError from getset descriptors)

PyPy 7.3.22 changed the exception type raised when accessing certain
getset descriptors on the type (rather than an instance): e.g.

instead of AttributeError. PyPy 7.3.21 and CPython still raise

getattr(obj, alias) call, so on PyPy 7.3.22 the new TypeError propagates

on the maintenance/4.0.x CI.

existing 'skip this alias' path (attach_dummy_node). Kept narrow on
purpose — only TypeError is added, not a bare Exception. CPython
behavior is unchanged because CPython still raises AttributeError.

problem_statement:
Fix RecursionError in _compute_mro() on circular class hierarchies (#2968)

* Fix circular MRO from name rebinding without raising errors

When a module-level name is rebound to a subclass of itself
(e.g. pdb.Pdb = CustomPdb where CustomPdb inherits from pdb.Pdb),
_infer_last follows the rebinding and returns the subclass as its
own base, causing infinite recursion in _compute_mro.

Instead of suppressing the RecursionError, resolve the cycle in
_inferred_bases by detecting when the inferred base is the class
itself and falling back to the first non-circular inferred value
from the base expression. This produces the correct MRO without
raising any errors.

Fixes #2967

subject: Resolve the type parameters of fields with the generic base declaring them (#4704)
problem_statement:
Resolve the type parameters of fields with the generic base declaring them (#4704)

* Resolve the type parameters of fields with the generic base declaring them

The arguments of a generic type's type parameters were looked up by name in
one map merged across all its generic bases, first base first. So a type like
`class LabelledPage(Page[int], Label[str])`, where both bases declare a
parameter named `T` (a shared `TypeVar` or two with the same name), gave every
inherited field `int`.

`get_generic_arguments()` now collects the arguments a class gives to the type
parameters of each of its generic bases, substituting arguments that use the
type parameters of the class extending a base, like `Box[list[U]]`. Field types
are resolved with the arguments of the class declaring the field first, then
with the merged map as before, so other existing uses keep working. A
`split_base` hook lets classes that aren't parametrized with `typing` aliases,
like Pydantic's generic models, reuse it.

* Resolve the arguments of generic bases like the ones of annotations

`get_base_type_var_map()` returned the arguments of a generic base as
they were written, so a field wrapping a type parameter, like
`content: list[T]`, got a `typing` alias like `list[int]` inside its
`StrawberryList`, which the schema can't convert.

The arguments of `Box[list[int]]` used in an annotation are resolved to
Strawberry types before they replace the type parameters, and now so are
the ones of a generic base. This also fixes arguments like `int | None`,
lazy types and generic types like `Edge[int]`, for subclasses like
`class IntListBox(Box[list[int]])`, which failed before too.

* Use realistic examples in the release notes

* Test a generic base given a type parameter of the same name

* Use the release notes' examples in get_generic_arguments' docstring

problem_statement:
Add a to_input hook to convert input instances to input values (#4658)

* Add a to_input hook to convert input instances to input values

Input instances used as argument and input field defaults are converted to
GraphQL input values with all their fields. Integrations that know better,
like strawberry.pydantic, which knows which fields of a model were set, had no
way to choose the fields, so a default like UserPatch(name="Ada") was turned
into a value that sets every other field to None.

StrawberryObjectDefinition.to_input, the counterpart of from_input, returns
the fields of an instance, keyed by python or GraphQL names. The schema
converter uses it when it converts defaults, and the fields it leaves out get
their default.

Shortcake-Parent: main

* Keep every field to_input returns, and call it for instances that are mappings

A None the hook returned for a field whose default is None was left out, like
for instances and dicts, so from_input couldn't tell an explicit null from an
omitted field. The hook decides which fields are present, so they're all kept
now, except UNSET ones.

The hook was also skipped for input instances that are mappings, which were
read like dict defaults.

subject: Resolve objects cast with strawberry.cast in unions (#4653)
problem_statement:
Resolve objects cast with strawberry.cast in unions (#4653)

* Resolve objects cast with strawberry.cast in unions

The union type resolver ignored strawberry.cast, so look-alike objects like
ORM rows couldn't be returned in unions. The cast now picks the member it's
cast to, including specializations of a generic type. When it doesn't match
exactly one member, for example a cast to an interface, the object is
resolved as before.

Shortcake-Parent: main

* Accept casts to a generic type in the is_type_of of its specializations

Types implementing an interface check the objects returned for them with a
generated is_type_of, which only accepted casts to the type itself or to its
interfaces. A specialization like IntEdge rejected an object cast to the
generic Edge, so returning it in a union, or through the interface, failed
with "Expected value of type 'IntEdge'".

* Raise an error for ambiguous casts to a generic type

A cast to a generic class, like strawberry.cast(Edge, row), matches every
specialization of it. When a union or an interface had more than one, like
Edge[int] | Edge[str], unions fell back to their regular resolution and
interfaces picked the first type whose is_type_of accepted the cast.

Both now raise AmbiguousCastError, through a get_cast_type_name helper that
unions and the interface type resolver share. Casts that match none of the
possible types, like casts to an interface, are still ignored.

subject: Fix DuplicatedTypeName for same-origin types (#4193)
problem_statement:
Fix DuplicatedTypeName for same-origin types (#4193)

* fix: false-positive DuplicatedTypeName for same-origin types

Add origin identity check in is_same_type_definition so that two
different StrawberryObjectDefinition instances sharing the same origin
class are recognized as the same type. This prevents false positives
when third-party decorators re-process a type.

Fix #4142

* test: replace synthetic tests with real lazy-import reproduction

Remove the two synthetic tests (proxy class with copied definition,
redundant same-name-different-origin check) and replace with a real
integration test that reproduces issue #4142 via lazy imports.

The new test triggers the actual bug path: a lazy import mid-schema-
construction re-decorates a type, replacing its __strawberry_definition__
after the original was already cached in the type_map.

* fix: handle DuplicatedTypeName false-positive after module reimport

When sys.modules is cleared (e.g. by test runners or Django reloaders),
reimporting a module creates new class objects with different id(). The
existing `origin is` check fails in this case, so fall back to comparing
__qualname__ and __module__ of the origin classes.

subject: Add support for nullable inputs and default values in schema codegen (#4178)
problem_statement:
Add support for nullable inputs and default values in schema codegen (#4178)

* feat(codegen): use Maybe for nullable input fields

schema-codegen now generates nullable input fields with
strawberry.Maybe[T | None] instead of just T | None.

This allows generated input types to be instantiated without
providing nullable fields, fixing the issue where empty inputs
like `{}` would cause TypeError.

Before:
```python
@strawberry.input
class HealthResultInput:
    some_number: int | None  # Required - causes TypeError
```

After:
```python
@strawberry.input
class HealthResultInput:
    some_number: strawberry.Maybe[int | None]  # Optional
```

Benefits of using Maybe over UNSET:
- Better type safety (proper generic type)
- Explicit nullability semantics
- Clearer distinction between absent and null values

* Add RELEASE.md

* Add support for defaults as well

subject: Fix lazy union types using new Annotated syntax (issue #4066) (#4156)
problem_statement:
Fix lazy union types using new Annotated syntax (issue #4066) (#4156)

* Fix lazy union types using new Annotated syntax (issue #4066)

When using the new recommended union syntax without explicit types argument:
  `MyUnion = Annotated[Union[A, B], strawberry.union("MyUnion")]`

The union would fail with "must define one or more member types" error
when used with lazy loading:
  `LazyUnion = Annotated["MyUnion", strawberry.lazy("module")]`

The issue was in `from_type()` which directly extracted the StrawberryUnion
from Annotated args. When created via the new syntax (without types=),
the StrawberryUnion has empty type_annotations. The fix now properly
extracts types from the Union[...] in the first Annotated argument and
creates a properly populated StrawberryUnion.

Added tests for:
- New syntax with pipe operator (TypeA | TypeB)
- New syntax with typing.Union
- Single-type unions (Union[TypeA])

* Add release file

subject: Keep PathAccessError printable for Scope/S paths (#249) (#298)
problem_statement:
Keep PathAccessError printable for Scope/S paths (#249) (#298)

PathAccessError.get_message() called Path(self.path) which re-wraps an
already-Path object. For S-rooted paths, Path() rejects the S root with
ValueError, crashing __str__ and producing '<exception str() failed>'.

Fix: call self.path.values() directly — self.path is already a Path at
every call site. Keep a lightweight AttributeError/IndexError fallback
for safety in case of unexpected .path types.

Test asserts the message content (key name, part index, error type),
not just that it doesn't crash.
